label: VERIFIED
extraction: Agent orchestration patterns conclusion: orchestration is a question of coordination cost rather than framework choice. Most tasks belong on lowest coordination level that works. Token costs scale linearly with agents; coordination failures scale worse than linearly. Cross-model consensus pattern sits outside single-vendor levels: running agents from different vendors against same problem and comparing outputs. Level 2 subagent failure: parallel orchestrator coordinating dozen workers collapsed in production (session limits, lost state, workers dying silently). Rule: move up a level only when current one demonstrably fails, never because parallelism sounds faster.
